items.title: Fable 5.2 is the best model in the world and I feel NOTHING. I'm so fucking done
items.summary:
Fable 5.2 is the best model in the world and I feel NOTHING. I'm so fucking done

It came out yesterday. I did not even run my shooter test on it.

Since July every new model built me a 3D shooter from 1 prompt. Kimi 3, Fable 5, GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5.5.
In September Opus 5.5 made a Blender scene and I asked out loud if this is AGI. I was in real shock.

Now I know the result before I press enter. A good shooter, yeah, im sure. I already have plenty of good shooters.

FrontierCode 2.0: Fable 5.2 gets 49.1%, Opus 5.5 gets 45.5%.
So what? Who cares about this?

The big demos now take over 1,000 agents and 8 days of compute. What actually changes for a dude like me with a single prompt? For me nothing changed since September.

And the timeline celebrates anyway. "This changes everything". The same thing was written about Opus 5.5 in September and about Astra before it. In a few weeks it will be written about the next one. 

I am tired of this race. Every few weeks there is a new number and a new round of hype, and I cannot name 1 thing I do differently because of it.

It makes me sad.

items.title: Anthropic has been receiving significant attention (Nov 6-8) following an independent evaluation report from METR. They'
items.summary:
Anthropic has been receiving significant attention (Nov 6-8) following an independent evaluation report from METR. They've found that their models have been improving at ~2x the previous rate on well-defined tasks (AECI benchmark: ~1.9x improvement since October 2025). The majority of this improvement is due to AI being used to aid their own R&D efforts. Employees using the flagship model internally claimed to see ~12x improvement in productivity. The release had heavy redactions.
Why this matters: This is the most explicit evidence we’ve seen of recursive improvement being done by a frontier lab. This accelerates capabilities timelines and raises safety concerns.
OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber (Nov 5) — a specialised variant of GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6 Cyber is rated as Critical within the OpenAI Preparedness Framework (previously High rating). It is only available to approved Daybreak Red customers. They have found 81 new high severity issues within Firefox. It has also contributed to creating exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities (588 novel) and has improved within its scope significantly.
Why this matters: This demonstrates how powerful dual-use cyber tools are seeing professional access. This will help improve defensive research.
OpenAI raised ~$11 billion in initial funding for a $1.25 trillion valuation (Nov 6). However this was lower than previous targets as the wider AI sector suffered a downturn.
Why this matters: This provides significant extra funding for compute and scaling. However, this demonstrates investor caution.
Thinking Machines Lab (Founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati) released Inkling 2 Small (Nov 5). This 594B parameter MoE model (17B active) focuses on agentic coding, vision and AI training automation. It has a score of 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It is currently available on their Tinker platform and will be released as Apache 2.0 following third party safety testing (Expected soon). They have also raised ~$5B with a ~$40B valuation (Unconfirmed).
Why this matters: This means we now have a well funded new competitor with an efficient MoE model. It focuses on meta tasks to improve model development.
Other noteworthy developments (not primary): Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available with longer video clips (Up to 15s) and reduced pricing. NVIDIA released Dory 1.0 — a small looping language model. World models continuing to improve within Robotics/Autonomy (Niantic pivot). Improvements in agent reliability. AI auditors can catch most of the misbehaviour but have very high false alarm rates. No major AI specific laws or policies were introduced. Anthropic are continuing to prepare for their IPO with a lower valuation range. There have been previous regulatory actions in the U.S. and internationally.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt.
